answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a tamper-evident beacon installed at a real address and inspected by an independent courier each season. A courier completes one inspection per day, so a farm cannot parallelize the process, and the inspection fee in outside money rises by a fixed delta per further beacon on the same funding trail. Each additional fake needs another real address, another beacon, another courier day, and a larger fee; anyone spinning a fable of extra deployments only grows the bill, and the quill-and-ink trail of the funding records exposes the cluster at a glance.
